title: Normalized slice evaluation of ordinary coherent scalar extension
statement: In the context of [def-pur-quotient-reduction-core], fix any normalized scalar model S for Delta R to B_bullet and normalized scalar models L_n for alpha_n:R to B_n [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. There is a natural isomorphism Delta followed by S.model.E followed by evaluation at n, to L_n.model.E, for every n. On the sheafified section 1 tensor x the isomorphism is the identity between the corresponding extension-unit sections. No flatness, K-flatness, or complex is assumed.

source.place: Step 2 and the evaluation-unit part of step 7 of lem-pur-quotient-system-flat-models; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, and Zheng Construction 4.1. This is the ordinary slice/sheafification calculation, with no homological assertions.

proof.text: Evaluate the sectionwise extension presheaf at the vertical slice n. Its sections and maps are exactly the extension along alpha_n. Restriction and vertical sheafification commute, yielding the natural isomorphism between the sheafified functors. Its inverse is the identity on the same balanced tensors. The existing restrictionSheafificationMap_isIso in SemilinearDerivedCalculus supplies this commutation for continuous cocontinuous slice restriction.

The natural isomorphism carries the sheafification unit on 1 tensor x to the sheafification unit on the identical tensor. The object equations in the two normalized models identify these units with scalarExtensionSection, proving the displayed normalization.

theorem quotientOrdinaryModels
    (scalar : ScalarData.{c, v, max c v r}
      (quotientRingMap.{c, v, r} J R B τ α hα))
    (levels : ∀ n : ℕ, ScalarData.{c, v, max c v r} (α n)) :
    ∃ reductionEvaluation : ∀ n : ℕ,
      quotientConstant.{c, v, r} J R ⋙ scalar.model.E ⋙
        evaluation.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n ≅ (levels n).model.E,
(∀ (M : Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J R) (n : ℕ) (U : Cᵒᵖ)
    (x : M.val.obj U)
    (y : ((evaluation.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n).obj
      (scalar.model.E.obj ((quotientConstant.{c, v, r} J R).obj M))).val.obj U),
    HEq y (scalarExtensionSection.{c, v, r} (quotientRingMap.{c, v, r} J R B τ α hα)
      scalar ((quotientConstant.{c, v, r} J R).obj M) (op (n, U.unop)) x) →
    HEq (((reductionEvaluation n).hom.app M).val.app U y)
      (scalarExtensionSection.{c, v, r} (α n) (levels n) M U x))
